members.name: get_base_model_state_dict
members.signature: get_base_model_state_dict(model: PeftModel)
members.summary: Return the base model's state dict, under the key names it had before it was adapted.
members.extended:
The adapters' tensors are left out, and the wrappers adapting put in the tree are
undone in the names: `q.base_layer.weight` comes back as `q.weight`, and
`head.original_module.weight` (a module saved in full) as `head.weight`.  The
tensors are the model's own, not copies.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: An adapted model, as `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` returns it.

returns.description: The base model's state dict.

raises.description: `model` is not a `PeftModel`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_base_model_state_dict, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4), nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> sorted(get_base_model_state_dict(peft))
['0.bias', '0.weight', '1.bias', '1.weight']

members.name: set_base_model_state_dict
members.signature: set_base_model_state_dict(model: PeftModel, state_dict: dict[str, Tensor], strict: bool = True)
members.summary: Load a state dict of the base model's original key names into an adapted model.
members.extended:
The counterpart of `lucid.peft.get_base_model_state_dict`: the keys are the ones the
model had before it was adapted (`q.weight`), and each is loaded into the place the
adapted model keeps that tensor (`q.base_layer.weight`).  The adapters' tensors
are not touched.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: An adapted model.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description: The base model's tensors by their original names.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description:
Raise when a base tensor is missing from `state_dict` or `state_dict` holds a
key the base model does not.

returns.description:
The base keys `state_dict` lacks (`missing_keys`) and the keys of `state_dict`
that match no base tensor (`unexpected_keys`).

raises.description: `model` is not a `PeftModel`.
`strict` is true and the keys do not match; nothing is loaded.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import (
...     LoraConfig, get_base_model_state_dict, get_peft_model, set_base_model_state_dict
... )
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4)), LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> weights = {k: lucid.zeros(*v.shape) for k, v in get_base_model_state_dict(peft).items()}
>>> set_base_model_state_dict(peft, weights)
_IncompatibleKeys(missing_keys=[], unexpected_keys=[])
>>> float(peft.get_base_model()[0].base_layer.weight.abs().sum())
0.0

methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is kept as the field it is.

The dict's `peft_type` picks the class, whichever class this is called
on, as the reference's `from_peft_type` does: `LoraConfig.from_dict` of
an OFT dict is an `OFTConfig`.  A dict that names no method is read as
the calling class (as LoRA on `PeftConfig`).

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description: `peft_type` names no method of this library.
The dict turns on a feature v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})
>>> type(LoraConfig.from_dict({"peft_type": "OFT", "target_modules": ["q"]})).__name__
'OFTConfig'

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(pretrained_model_name_or_path: str | os.PathLike[str], subfolder: str | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Read `adapter_config.json` from a local adapter directory.
methods.extended:
The file's `peft_type` picks the config class, whichever class this is called
on (`PeftConfig.from_pretrained` of a LoRA adapter is a `LoraConfig`, and
`LoraConfig.from_pretrained` of an OFT adapter an `OFTConfig`), as the
reference's does.  The file's keys go through that class's `check_kwargs`
first, before any is dropped for being unknown, and then through `from_dict`.
The reference calls the `check_kwargs` of the class this is called on, which is
the file's class on the paths that load a model; here it is the file's class on
every path, so an OFT file is checked when read through `PeftConfig` too.

parameters.name: pretrained_model_name_or_path
parameters.description:
A directory holding `adapter_config.json` — one written by
`save_pretrained` or by the reference library.  Hub ids
are not resolved; download the adapter first.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
A directory under `pretrained_model_name_or_path` that holds
the file, e.g. the sub-directory `save_pretrained` gives each
adapter but the one named `"default"`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`,
`token`, `cache_dir` …).  Adapters are read from a local
directory, so any key given here raises.

returns.description: The config, read through `from_dict`, of the class the file's `peft_type` names.

raises.description: The directory has no `adapter_config.json`.

The file does not hold a JSON object, or its class's `check_kwargs` refuses it
(an OFT file of the reference's before 0.14.0).
The file's `peft_type` names no method of this library.
`kwargs` is not empty, or the file turns on a feature this library lacks.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules="all-linear").save_pretrained(d)
...     loaded = LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d)
>>> loaded.r, loaded.lora_alpha, loaded.target_modules
(16, 32, 'all-linear')

warns.description:
The file's class's `check_kwargs` warns (an OFT file of the reference's before

field for.

methods.name: from_peft_type
methods.summary: Build a config from its fields given as keyword arguments, the class chosen by `peft_type`.
methods.extended:
The reference's way to turn the keys of a config file into a config: the
`peft_type` argument names the method and so the class, whichever class this is
called on.  Without one, the calling class is built.  The fields are read as
`from_dict` reads them, so a key this library has no field for is accepted
at a value that turns its feature off (dropped, with a warning when the key is
unknown), where the reference drops it at any value.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description: The config's fields, by name; `peft_type` is a `PeftType` or its string.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class `peft_type` names.

raises.description: `peft_type` names no method of this library.
No `peft_type` is given and this is `PeftConfig` itself, which builds no config of its own.
A key turns on a feature this library does not implement.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> config = PeftConfig.from_peft_type(peft_type="LORA", r=4, target_modules=["q"])
>>> type(config).__name__, config.r
('LoraConfig', 4)
>>> LoraConfig.from_peft_type(r=2, target_modules=["q"]).r
2

members.name: PeftType
members.signature: PeftType()
members.summary: The parameter-efficient method an adapter file holds.
members.extended:
The members are the reference library's `peft_type` strings, so a
config file names its method the same way on both sides.
Every member has a config class that reads and writes `adapter_config.json`, and every one
but `SHADOW` has an adapter that can be built.  The first twenty-six: the LoRA family
(`LORA`, `ADALORA`), the
orthogonal and LyCORIS families (`OFT`, `BOFT`, `HRA`, `LOHA`, `LOKR`), the shared-table
tuners (`VERA`, `VBLORA`, `RANDLORA`), the structured and sparse updates (`MISS`, its
predecessor `BONE`, `SHIRA`, `C3A`, `FOURIERFT`), `IA3`, `LN_TUNING`,
`TRAINABLE_TOKENS`, the prompt-learning methods (`PROMPT_TUNING`,
`MULTITASK_PROMPT_TUNING`, `PREFIX_TUNING`, `P_TUNING`, `CPT`), the adaption prompt
(`ADAPTION_PROMPT`) and the routing and mixing methods (`POLY`, `XLORA`).  The other
nineteen are the methods the reference library added since (`DELORA` … `ADAMSS`; see
`lucid.peft.tuners`).  `SHADOW` is refused for good: building it raises
`NotImplementedError`.  A file that names a type no config reads raises
`NotImplementedError`.

members.extended:
Prompt tuning, prefix tuning and p-tuning put learned vectors in front
of the input — as extra token embeddings, or as extra keys and values
of every attention layer.  The sizes they need are the base model's, so
everything but `num_virtual_tokens` can be left `None` and is read
off the model's `config` when the adapter is built.

members.extended:
It chooses the model class `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` and

members.name: NoMatchingPeftModuleError
members.signature: NoMatchingPeftModuleError()
members.summary: An adapter's targets matched no module, or no parameter, of the model.
members.extended:
Raised when `target_modules` (or `target_parameters`, or
`modules_to_save`) selects nothing, which most often points at a
misconfiguration.  It subclasses `ValueError`, which was raised before it
existed, so `except ValueError` keeps catching it; code that adds such an
adapter on purpose can catch this class (or `PeftError`) and go on.
examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, NoMatchingPeftModuleError, get_peft_model
>>> try:
...     get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 2)), LoraConfig(target_modules=["missing"]))
... except NoMatchingPeftModuleError as error:
...     isinstance(error, ValueError)
True

for a bad argument.
examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import NoMatchingPeftModuleError, PeftError
>>> issubclass(NoMatchingPeftModuleError, PeftError)

members.name: find_kappa_target_modules
members.signature: find_kappa_target_modules(model: nn.Module, top_p: float = 0.2, max_dim_size_to_analyze: int = 16384, moe_param_suffixes: tuple[str, ...] | None = None, show_progress: bool = True)
members.summary: Choose what to adapt by the condition number of the weights (KappaTune).
members.extended:
The condition number of a weight matrix is its largest singular value over its
smallest.  The `top_p` fraction of `nn.Linear` modules with the lowest numbers
are returned as `target_modules`, and the same fraction of the fused
mixture-of-experts weights (three-dimensional parameters named `gate_up_proj`,
`down_proj` and the like) as `target_parameters`, a pair ready to give to
`lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.  An expert weight's number is the mean over its
experts.  Every weight is decomposed, so a large model takes a while.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The base model whose weights are analysed.

parameters.name: top_p
parameters.description:
The fraction, between 0 and 1, of candidates to keep; at least one is kept
when there are any.

parameters.name: max_dim_size_to_analyze
parameters.description: A weight with a dimension larger than this is skipped.

parameters.name: moe_param_suffixes
parameters.description:
The endings of the names of fused expert parameters; `.gate_up_proj`,
`.down_proj`, `.gate_proj` and `.up_proj` when `None`.

parameters.name: show_progress
parameters.description: Accepted for the reference's signature; no progress bar is drawn.

returns.annotation: dict of str to list of str or None
returns.description:
`{"target_modules": [...], "target_parameters": [...] or None}`; the second is
`None` when the model has no fused expert weights.

raises.description: `top_p` is outside `[0, 1]`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import find_kappa_target_modules
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.Linear(8, 8))
>>> picked = find_kappa_target_modules(net, top_p=0.4)
>>> len(picked["target_modules"]), picked["target_parameters"]
(1, None)

members.name: get_peft_model
members.signature: get_peft_model(model: nn.Module, peft_config: PeftConfig, adapter_name: str = 'default', mixed: bool = False, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True, revision: str | None = None, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False)
members.summary: Adapt `model` with the method `peft_config` names and return it wrapped as a `lucid.peft.PeftModel` (or, with `mixed=True`, a `lucid.peft.PeftMixedModel`).
members.extended:
The model is changed in place: each module `peft_config` selects
becomes an adapter layer of that method (LoRA, (IA)^3, LoHa, LoKr) around the
original, and every parameter but the adapter's is frozen.  `peft_config`
is not changed — the wrapper keeps a copy — with two additions the reference makes too: a
`base_model_name_or_path` read from the model's `name_or_path`,
when it has one, and, for a classification or question-answering
`task_type`, the model's `classifier` / `score` / `qa_outputs`
head added to `modules_to_save` so that it trains.

`PeftModelForCausalLM` for `"CAUSAL_LM"`, `PeftModelForSeq2SeqLM`,
`PeftModelForSequenceClassification`, `PeftModelForTokenClassification`,
`PeftModelForQuestionAnswering` and `PeftModelForFeatureExtraction`
for theirs (`MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING` is the table), and a
plain `PeftModel` when the config has no task.  With `mixed=True` it is always a
`PeftMixedModel` whatever the task, which holds the adapters of several methods at once.

members.summary: A model holding the adapters of several methods at once, loaded from files and not saved.
members.extended:
The first adapter of a method puts that method's layer on each module it targets; the layers of
other methods stand on it, so the forward pass runs them lowest first.  The tuner is a
`lucid.peft.tuners.MixedModel`, kept as `base_model` (the user's model is
`base_model.model`), and the state dict reads `base_model.model....` as a
`lucid.peft.PeftModel`'s does.  Calling it runs the wrapped model, and any public name
it lacks is read from that model, so code written for the bare model keeps working.

It is not a `PeftModel`: there is no task wrapper, no `adapter_names` routing of a batch
and no `save_pretrained`.  An adapter is written by the `PeftModel` of its own method
and read here with `load_adapter` or `from_pretrained`, which fill it from the
single-method file, before or after the layers of other methods are stacked on it.  The
reference's mixed model writes nothing either, and says so with the same `NotImplementedError`.

The methods that can be mixed are the keys of
`PEFT_TYPE_TO_MIXED_MODEL_MAPPING`; any other is refused with `ValueError` where it is
added.  Adding an adapter that cannot sit where it would land raises
`ValueError` and leaves the model as it was.  AdaLoRA takes part for inference only.

members.extended:
The preparation step run before training an adapter on a base model loaded for
low-memory or k-bit training: every parameter stops requiring a gradient (the adapter
adds its own), and each `float16` or `bfloat16` parameter becomes `float32`, so
that the layer norms, embeddings, and output head compute at full precision.  When the
model is quantized (`lucid.nn.quantized.QuantizedLinearMLX`,
`lucid.nn.quantized.Linear`, `lucid.nn.quantized.dynamic.Linear`, or
`is_loaded_in_4bit` / `is_loaded_in_8bit`) and `use_gradient_checkpointing` is
`True`, input embeddings are configured to require gradients and
`gradient_checkpointing_enable` is invoked if the model provides it.  The model is
changed in place and returned.

members.summary: Hold `module` beside a trained copy per adapter; the active adapter's copy runs.
members.extended:
Building one changes nothing about `module` — the tuner builds them
while it is still planning, and a plan that fails must leave the model
as it was.  Which of the copies train is the tuner's freezing step.  It
answers the tuner's `_AdapterSlot` protocol, as a tuner layer does.

At most one adapter is active here: two copies of one module would have
no rule for whose weights the forward pass uses.  `active_adapter` is
the active adapter that has a copy, or `""` when none does, in which
case the original runs.

`get_peft_model(..., modules_to_save=[...])` puts one of these where each
named module was, so `isinstance(m, ModulesToSaveWrapper)` finds them in an
adapted model.  The module as the base model had it is `original_module`,
and the trained copies are in the `modules_to_save` dict, keyed by adapter.

parameters.name: adapter_name

>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], modules_to_save=["1"])
>>> _ = get_peft_model(net, config)
>>> head = net[1]
>>> isinstance(head, ModulesToSaveWrapper), head.active_adapter
(True, 'default')
>>> head.get_base_layer() is head.original_module, list(head.modules_to_save)
(True, ['default'])

parameters.description: Positional arguments of the model's `forward`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
Keyword arguments of the model's `forward`, and two of the adapter's own:

`adapter_names` (sequence of str)
    One adapter per row of the batch (the first dimension of the
    inputs): row `i` is computed with `adapter_names[i]` alone,
    `"__base__"` for the base model, all in one pass, so requests
    for different adapters can share a batch.  The adapters in use
    are ignored.  Inference only, for LoRA on `nn.Linear`,
    `nn.Embedding` and convolution layers (and `modules_to_save`
    modules).
`task_ids` (Tensor)
    For multitask prompt tuning: the task of each row of the batch, `(batch,)`
    integers in `[0, num_tasks)`, whose prompt is put in front of that row.

returns.description: What the model's `forward` returns.

raises.description:
`adapter_names` is given in training mode, names an adapter
the model lacks, a row count other than the batch's, or the
model holds merged adapters or a DoRA adapter among those named;
`task_ids` is given to an adapter whose prompt is not made per task.

The method is not LoRA, or the model has an adapted layer a
mixed batch cannot route (attention, a raw parameter).

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, config, adapter_name="a")
>>> peft.add_adapter("b", config)
>>> _ = peft.eval()
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> mixed = peft(x, adapter_names=["a", "b", "__base__"])
>>> peft.set_adapter("b")
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(mixed[1], peft(x)[1], atol=1e-6))
True

methods.name: disable_adapter

methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.

...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())

methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: save_embedding_layers
parameters.description:
The reference saves the input and output embeddings beside the adapter when the
vocabulary was resized.  Here an adapter file holds the adapter alone (and its
`modules_to_save`), so `"auto"` and `False` write that; `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: is_main_process
parameters.description:
`False` writes nothing, for the processes of a distributed run that are not the
main one.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub upload.  Any key raises
`NotImplementedError`.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`, `save_embedding_layers=True`, or a key in `kwargs`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> base_state = {k: v.clone() for k, v in net.state_dict().items()}
>>> trained = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                         init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)

...     trained.save_pretrained(d)
...     fresh = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)
...     loaded = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh, d)

members.extended:
Wraps the model in its method's tuner (`LoraModel` for a
`LoraConfig`), kept as `base_model` (the user's model is
`base_model.model`), so the
state dict reads `base_model.model....lora_A.default.weight` and the
adapter file `base_model.model....lora_A.weight`, the reference
library's layouts.  Calling it runs the wrapped model, and any public
name it lacks — `generate`, `config`, a head — is read from that
model, so code written for the bare model keeps working.

`load_adapter` bring one in beside the others (frozen and inactive),
`set_adapter` switches which one the model computes with — and
trains — and `delete_adapter` drops one.  `save_pretrained` writes
them all, the `"default"` one at the directory itself and each other
in a sub-directory of its own name.

`from_pretrained` for a saved adapter.  Both pick the class from the
config's `task_type`: the wrappers (`PeftModelForCausalLM` and the
others, `MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING`) are subclasses of this
one, each registered for its task by `class Wrapper(PeftModel,
task_type=TaskType.X)`; an adapter with no task, or a task no wrapper
is registered for, gets this class itself.

members.signature: bloom_model_postprocess_past_key_value(past_key_values: tuple[Tensor, ...])
members.summary: Reshape a prefix-tuning prompt into the cache layout of the bloom family.
members.extended:
The bloom family keeps its keys as `(batch * heads, head_dim, tokens)` and its
values as `(batch * heads, tokens, head_dim)`.  This joins the prompt's tensors
along their first axis, takes the first half of the result for keys and the second
half for values, and reshapes each to that layout — the reference's rule, split
point included.

parameters.description:

the `n` of all of them add up to an even number of layers' keys and values.

returns.description: One `(keys, values)` pair per layer.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.peft import bloom_model_postprocess_past_key_value
>>> prompt = tuple(lucid.zeros(1, 2, 4, 3, 8) for _ in range(4))  # 2 layers: keys, then values
>>> pairs = bloom_model_postprocess_past_key_value(prompt)
>>> len(pairs), pairs[0][0].shape, pairs[0][1].shape
(2, (8, 8, 3), (8, 3, 8))

members.summary: Load an adapter's tensors, keyed as an adapter file keys them, into `model`.
members.extended:
Each key is mapped back to where the tensor lives in memory (the
adapter name put back in) and copied into the existing parameter,
which keeps its dtype, device and identity.  Every key is checked
before anything is copied: one that lands nowhere, or a shape that
differs, raises with the model untouched — an adapter loaded into the
wrong model must not pass for a fresh one.  An adapter tensor the dict
does not supply is reported in a warning and keeps its value.

`NotImplementedError`.

`ignore_mismatched_sizes` or `low_cpu_mem_usage` is `True`.

>>> from lucid.peft import (LoraConfig, get_peft_model,
...                         get_peft_model_state_dict, set_peft_model_state_dict)
>>> make = lambda: get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                               LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False))

methods.name: disable_adapter
methods.summary: Run the base model alone inside the `with` block.
methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.

...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())

methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: save_embedding_layers
parameters.description:
The reference saves the input and output embeddings beside the adapter when the
vocabulary was resized.  Here an adapter file holds the adapter alone (and its
`modules_to_save`), so `"auto"` and `False` write that; `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: is_main_process
parameters.description:
`False` writes nothing, for the processes of a distributed run that are not the
main one.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub upload.  Any key raises
`NotImplementedError`.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`, `save_embedding_layers=True`, or a key in `kwargs`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(model: nn.Module, model_id: str | os.PathLike[str], adapter_name: str = 'default', is_trainable: bool = False, config: PeftConfig | None = None, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True, ephemeral_gpu_offload: bool = False, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, key_mapping: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, subfolder: str | None = None, convert: ConvertMode = 'auto', kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model

>>> base_state = {k: v.clone() for k, v in net.state_dict().items()}

...                                         init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     trained.save_pretrained(d)
...     fresh = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)
...     loaded = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh, d)
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(loaded(x), trained(x)))

methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter is initialised, not trained, and starts frozen and inactive: the model
computes what it computed, and every parameter keeps its `requires_grad`.  Switch to it
with `set_adapter`.  Modules an earlier adapter wraps take the new one beside it; a
classification or question-answering `task_type` adds the model's head to
`modules_to_save` as `get_peft_model` does.  Merged layers stay merged, and the adapter
starts from their weights as they were before the merge.

the case here; `False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

would train biases, or a PiSSA / OLoRA / LoRA-GA start would write the base weights of
merged layers (`base_model.unmerge_adapter()` first).  The model is left as it was.

>>> import lucid

methods.name: disable_adapter
methods.summary: Run the base model alone inside the `with` block.
methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.
examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 4)
>>> base_out = net(x)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())
True

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.signature: save_pretrained(save_directory: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True, selected_adapters: list[str] | None = None, save_embedding_layers: bool | Literal['auto'] = 'auto', is_main_process: bool = True, path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: save_embedding_layers
parameters.description:
The reference saves the input and output embeddings beside the adapter when the
vocabulary was resized.  Here an adapter file holds the adapter alone (and its
`modules_to_save`), so `"auto"` and `False` write that; `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: is_main_process
parameters.description:
`False` writes nothing, for the processes of a distributed run that are not the
main one.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub upload.  Any key raises
`NotImplementedError`.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`, `save_embedding_layers=True`, or a key in `kwargs`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(model: nn.Module, model_id: str | os.PathLike[str], adapter_name: str = 'default', is_trainable: bool = False, config: PeftConfig | None = None, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True, ephemeral_gpu_offload: bool = False, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, key_mapping: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, subfolder: str | None = None, convert: ConvertMode = 'auto', kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

parameters.description: A local adapter directory.  Hub ids are not resolved.

parameters.description: Name to give the adapter.

Keep the adapter trainable.  By default it is frozen and the
model is put in `eval()` mode, for inference.

parameters.description:
Cast a half-precision base's adapter weights to float32.  Always the case here;
`False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: ephemeral_gpu_offload
parameters.description: Not implemented: `True` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Build the adapter on the meta device.  Not implemented: `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: key_mapping
parameters.description:
Renames the adapter file's keys before they are loaded: for each key, with its
`base_model.model.` prefix set aside, the first pattern (a regular expression)
that matches is replaced by its value, as the reference does.  Applied before
`convert`.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
The directory under `model_id` that holds the adapter.  (The reference takes
it among `**kwargs`; it is named here.)

parameters.name: convert
parameters.description:
Convert an adapter written for the reference library's model to the
zoo model's layout (`lucid.peft` lists what each converter does):
`gpt2` (the `score` head), `roformer`, `t5` (renamed
modules) and `vit` (`query` / `key` / `value` fused into
`qkv`, LoRA only).  `"auto"` converts when the model's type has
a converter and the file is in a layout it changes; `True` always
converts and refuses a type with none; `False` reads it as it is.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`, `token`,
`cache_dir` …).  Any key raises `NotImplementedError`.

`model`, adapted and loaded — a task wrapper if the adapter
names a task.

raises.description: The directory lacks `adapter_config.json` or the weights.

The weights are a pickle (`adapter_model.bin`), the config
describes something lucid.peft does not implement, or an option the
library cannot honour is set (see the parameters).
The adapter's tensors do not fit `model`, or `convert` cannot apply.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> base_state = {k: v.clone() for k, v in net.state_dict().items()}
>>> trained = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                         init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     trained.save_pretrained(d)
...     fresh = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)
...     loaded = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh, d)
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(loaded(x), trained(x)))
True

The new adapter is initialised, not trained, and starts frozen and inactive: the model
computes what it computed, and every parameter keeps its `requires_grad`.  Switch to it
with `set_adapter`.  Modules an earlier adapter wraps take the new one beside it; a
classification or question-answering `task_type` adds the model's head to
`modules_to_save` as `get_peft_model` does.  Merged layers stay merged, and the adapter
starts from their weights as they were before the merge.

methods.name: disable_adapter
methods.summary: Run the base model alone inside the `with` block.
methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.

>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.signature: save_pretrained(save_directory: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True, selected_adapters: list[str] | None = None, save_embedding_layers: bool | Literal['auto'] = 'auto', is_main_process: bool = True, path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: save_embedding_layers
parameters.description:
The reference saves the input and output embeddings beside the adapter when the
vocabulary was resized.  Here an adapter file holds the adapter alone (and its
`modules_to_save`), so `"auto"` and `False` write that; `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: is_main_process
parameters.description:
`False` writes nothing, for the processes of a distributed run that are not the
main one.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub upload.  Any key raises
`NotImplementedError`.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`, `save_embedding_layers=True`, or a key in `kwargs`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(model: nn.Module, model_id: str | os.PathLike[str], adapter_name: str = 'default', is_trainable: bool = False, config: PeftConfig | None = None, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True, ephemeral_gpu_offload: bool = False, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, key_mapping: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, subfolder: str | None = None, convert: ConvertMode = 'auto', kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

parameters.description: The base model the adapter was trained on.

parameters.name: model_id
parameters.description: A local adapter directory.  Hub ids are not resolved.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name to give the adapter.

parameters.name: is_trainable
parameters.description:
Keep the adapter trainable.  By default it is frozen and the
model is put in `eval()` mode, for inference.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Use this config instead of the directory's.

parameters.name: autocast_adapter_dtype
parameters.description:
Cast a half-precision base's adapter weights to float32.  Always the case here;
`False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: ephemeral_gpu_offload
parameters.description: Not implemented: `True` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Build the adapter on the meta device.  Not implemented: `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: key_mapping
parameters.description:
Renames the adapter file's keys before they are loaded: for each key, with its
`base_model.model.` prefix set aside, the first pattern (a regular expression)
that matches is replaced by its value, as the reference does.  Applied before
`convert`.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
The directory under `model_id` that holds the adapter.  (The reference takes
it among `**kwargs`; it is named here.)

parameters.name: convert
parameters.description:
Convert an adapter written for the reference library's model to the
zoo model's layout (`lucid.peft` lists what each converter does):
`gpt2` (the `score` head), `roformer`, `t5` (renamed
modules) and `vit` (`query` / `key` / `value` fused into
`qkv`, LoRA only).  `"auto"` converts when the model's type has
a converter and the file is in a layout it changes; `True` always
converts and refuses a type with none; `False` reads it as it is.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`, `token`,
`cache_dir` …).  Any key raises `NotImplementedError`.

returns.description:
`model`, adapted and loaded — a task wrapper if the adapter
names a task.

raises.description: The directory lacks `adapter_config.json` or the weights.

The weights are a pickle (`adapter_model.bin`), the config
describes something lucid.peft does not implement, or an option the
library cannot honour is set (see the parameters).
The adapter's tensors do not fit `model`, or `convert` cannot apply.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> base_state = {k: v.clone() for k, v in net.state_dict().items()}
>>> trained = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                         init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     trained.save_pretrained(d)
...     fresh = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)
...     loaded = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh, d)
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(loaded(x), trained(x)))
True

methods.extended:
For a prompt-learning adapter: `True` unless inside `disable_adapter()`.  For the other
methods the reference also answers `True` when no adapter is in use, so inside
`disable_adapter()` the answer is `False` only while an adapter is in use.

methods.name: prepare_model_for_gradient_checkpointing
methods.summary: Make a model's embedding output require a gradient, so a checkpointed stack trains.
methods.extended:
What `use_reentrant=True` checkpointing needs when the embeddings are frozen: the segment
has an input that requires a gradient.  A model with `enable_input_require_grads` is asked
to; otherwise a forward hook on its input embeddings (or, with none, a pre-hook on the model
itself) marks the first floating-point tensor.  A quantized model is left as it is.  Unlike
the reference, the constructor does not call this: no Lucid model reports
`is_gradient_checkpointing`, and the default `use_reentrant=False` needs nothing.

>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["1"]))
>>> peft.prepare_model_for_gradient_checkpointing(net) is net
True

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.signature: add_adapter(adapter_name: str, peft_config: PeftConfig, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True)
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter is initialised, not trained, and starts frozen and inactive: the model
computes what it computed, and every parameter keeps its `requires_grad`.  Switch to it
with `set_adapter`.  Modules an earlier adapter wraps take the new one beside it; a
classification or question-answering `task_type` adds the model's head to
`modules_to_save` as `get_peft_model` does.  Merged layers stay merged, and the adapter
starts from their weights as they were before the merge.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the new adapter; unique among the model's adapters.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Build the adapter on the meta device.  Not implemented: `True`
raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: autocast_adapter_dtype
parameters.description:
Cast a half-precision base's adapter weights to float32.  Always
the case here; `False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

raises.description:
The name is taken, the config is another method's, no module matches it, two adapters
would train biases, or a PiSSA / OLoRA / LoRA-GA start would write the base weights of
merged layers (`base_model.unmerge_adapter()` first).  The model is left as it was.

`low_cpu_mem_usage` or `autocast_adapter_dtype` holds a value
the library cannot honour.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4), nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("second", LoraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["0", "1"]))
>>> peft.active_adapter, sorted(peft.peft_config)
('default', ['default', 'second'])
>>> peft.set_adapter("second")
>>> peft.get_base_model()[1].lora_A["second"].weight.shape
(4, 4)

methods.name: disable_adapter
methods.summary: Run the base model alone inside the `with` block.
methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.
examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 4)
>>> base_out = net(x)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())
True

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Fold the adapter(s) into the base model and hand the base model back.
methods.extended:
For deployment: the result runs at the base model's cost and saves,
exports and compiles as an ordinary model.  This wrapper is spent
afterwards, and adapters that were not folded in are gone with it.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Kept for call compatibility with the reference; ignored.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description:
Refuse, before changing any weight, if a merged weight would
hold NaN or inf.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Which adapters to fold in; the ones in use by default.

returns.description: `get_base_model()`, with plain `nn.Linear` layers again.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module (a tied head),
or a `modules_to_save` module was trained apart from a tie.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> adapted = peft(x)
>>> plain = peft.merge_and_unload()
>>> type(plain[0]) is nn.Linear, bool(lucid.allclose(plain(x), adapted, atol=1e-5))
(True, True)

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.signature: save_pretrained(save_directory: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True, selected_adapters: list[str] | None = None, save_embedding_layers: bool | Literal['auto'] = 'auto', is_main_process: bool = True, path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: save_embedding_layers
parameters.description:
The reference saves the input and output embeddings beside the adapter when the
vocabulary was resized.  Here an adapter file holds the adapter alone (and its
`modules_to_save`), so `"auto"` and `False` write that; `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: is_main_process
parameters.description:
`False` writes nothing, for the processes of a distributed run that are not the
main one.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub upload.  Any key raises
`NotImplementedError`.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`, `save_embedding_layers=True`, or a key in `kwargs`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(model: nn.Module, model_id: str | os.PathLike[str], adapter_name: str = 'default', is_trainable: bool = False, config: PeftConfig | None = None, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True, ephemeral_gpu_offload: bool = False, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, key_mapping: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, subfolder: str | None = None, convert: ConvertMode = 'auto', kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The base model the adapter was trained on.

parameters.name: model_id
parameters.description: A local adapter directory.  Hub ids are not resolved.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name to give the adapter.

parameters.name: is_trainable
parameters.description:
Keep the adapter trainable.  By default it is frozen and the
model is put in `eval()` mode, for inference.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Use this config instead of the directory's.

parameters.name: autocast_adapter_dtype
parameters.description:
Cast a half-precision base's adapter weights to float32.  Always the case here;
`False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: ephemeral_gpu_offload
parameters.description: Not implemented: `True` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Build the adapter on the meta device.  Not implemented: `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: key_mapping
parameters.description:
Renames the adapter file's keys before they are loaded: for each key, with its
`base_model.model.` prefix set aside, the first pattern (a regular expression)
that matches is replaced by its value, as the reference does.  Applied before
`convert`.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
The directory under `model_id` that holds the adapter.  (The reference takes
it among `**kwargs`; it is named here.)

parameters.name: convert
parameters.description:
Convert an adapter written for the reference library's model to the
zoo model's layout (`lucid.peft` lists what each converter does):
`gpt2` (the `score` head), `roformer`, `t5` (renamed
modules) and `vit` (`query` / `key` / `value` fused into
`qkv`, LoRA only).  `"auto"` converts when the model's type has
a converter and the file is in a layout it changes; `True` always
converts and refuses a type with none; `False` reads it as it is.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`, `token`,
`cache_dir` …).  Any key raises `NotImplementedError`.

returns.description:
`model`, adapted and loaded — a task wrapper if the adapter
names a task.

raises.description: The directory lacks `adapter_config.json` or the weights.

The weights are a pickle (`adapter_model.bin`), the config
describes something lucid.peft does not implement, or an option the
library cannot honour is set (see the parameters).
The adapter's tensors do not fit `model`, or `convert` cannot apply.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> base_state = {k: v.clone() for k, v in net.state_dict().items()}
>>> trained = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                         init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     trained.save_pretrained(d)
...     fresh = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)
...     loaded = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh, d)
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(loaded(x), trained(x)))
True

has an input that requires a gradient.  A model with `enable_input_require_grads` is asked

itself) marks the first floating-point tensor.  A quantized model is left as it is.  Unlike
the reference, the constructor does not call this: no Lucid model reports
`is_gradient_checkpointing`, and the default `use_reentrant=False` needs nothing.

methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter is initialised, not trained, and starts frozen and inactive: the model
computes what it computed, and every parameter keeps its `requires_grad`.  Switch to it
with `set_adapter`.  Modules an earlier adapter wraps take the new one beside it; a
classification or question-answering `task_type` adds the model's head to
`modules_to_save` as `get_peft_model` does.  Merged layers stay merged, and the adapter
starts from their weights as they were before the merge.

parameters.name: peft_config

Build the adapter on the meta device.  Not implemented: `True`
raises `NotImplementedError`.

Cast a half-precision base's adapter weights to float32.  Always
the case here; `False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

The name is taken, the config is another method's, no module matches it, two adapters
would train biases, or a PiSSA / OLoRA / LoRA-GA start would write the base weights of
merged layers (`base_model.unmerge_adapter()` first).  The model is left as it was.

`low_cpu_mem_usage` or `autocast_adapter_dtype` holds a value
the library cannot honour.

>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn

>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("second", LoraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["0", "1"]))
>>> peft.active_adapter, sorted(peft.peft_config)
('default', ['default', 'second'])
>>> peft.set_adapter("second")
>>> peft.get_base_model()[1].lora_A["second"].weight.shape

methods.name: disable_adapter
methods.summary: Run the base model alone inside the `with` block.
methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.
examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 4)
>>> base_out = net(x)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())
True

methods.summary: Fold the adapter(s) into the base model and hand the base model back.
methods.extended:
For deployment: the result runs at the base model's cost and saves,
exports and compiles as an ordinary model.  This wrapper is spent
afterwards, and adapters that were not folded in are gone with it.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Kept for call compatibility with the reference; ignored.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description:
Refuse, before changing any weight, if a merged weight would
hold NaN or inf.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Which adapters to fold in; the ones in use by default.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module (a tied head),
or a `modules_to_save` module was trained apart from a tie.

>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.signature: save_pretrained(save_directory: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True, selected_adapters: list[str] | None = None, save_embedding_layers: bool | Literal['auto'] = 'auto', is_main_process: bool = True, path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: save_embedding_layers
parameters.description:
The reference saves the input and output embeddings beside the adapter when the
vocabulary was resized.  Here an adapter file holds the adapter alone (and its
`modules_to_save`), so `"auto"` and `False` write that; `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: is_main_process
parameters.description:
`False` writes nothing, for the processes of a distributed run that are not the
main one.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub upload.  Any key raises
`NotImplementedError`.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`, `save_embedding_layers=True`, or a key in `kwargs`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(model: nn.Module, model_id: str | os.PathLike[str], adapter_name: str = 'default', is_trainable: bool = False, config: PeftConfig | None = None, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True, ephemeral_gpu_offload: bool = False, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, key_mapping: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, subfolder: str | None = None, convert: ConvertMode = 'auto', kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

parameters.description: The base model the adapter was trained on.

parameters.name: model_id
parameters.description: A local adapter directory.  Hub ids are not resolved.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name to give the adapter.

parameters.name: is_trainable
parameters.description:
Keep the adapter trainable.  By default it is frozen and the
model is put in `eval()` mode, for inference.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Use this config instead of the directory's.

parameters.name: autocast_adapter_dtype
parameters.description:
Cast a half-precision base's adapter weights to float32.  Always the case here;
`False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: ephemeral_gpu_offload
parameters.description: Not implemented: `True` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Build the adapter on the meta device.  Not implemented: `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: key_mapping
parameters.description:
Renames the adapter file's keys before they are loaded: for each key, with its
`base_model.model.` prefix set aside, the first pattern (a regular expression)
that matches is replaced by its value, as the reference does.  Applied before
`convert`.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
The directory under `model_id` that holds the adapter.  (The reference takes
it among `**kwargs`; it is named here.)

parameters.name: convert
parameters.description:
Convert an adapter written for the reference library's model to the
zoo model's layout (`lucid.peft` lists what each converter does):
`gpt2` (the `score` head), `roformer`, `t5` (renamed
modules) and `vit` (`query` / `key` / `value` fused into
`qkv`, LoRA only).  `"auto"` converts when the model's type has
a converter and the file is in a layout it changes; `True` always
converts and refuses a type with none; `False` reads it as it is.

parameters.name: **kwargs

The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`, `token`,

`model`, adapted and loaded — a task wrapper if the adapter
names a task.

The weights are a pickle (`adapter_model.bin`), the config
describes something lucid.peft does not implement, or an option the
library cannot honour is set (see the parameters).
The adapter's tensors do not fit `model`, or `convert` cannot apply.

>>> import tempfile
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> base_state = {k: v.clone() for k, v in net.state_dict().items()}
>>> trained = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                         init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     trained.save_pretrained(d)
...     fresh = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)
...     loaded = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh, d)
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(loaded(x), trained(x)))
True

methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter is initialised, not trained, and starts frozen and inactive: the model
computes what it computed, and every parameter keeps its `requires_grad`.  Switch to it
with `set_adapter`.  Modules an earlier adapter wraps take the new one beside it; a
classification or question-answering `task_type` adds the model's head to
`modules_to_save` as `get_peft_model` does.  Merged layers stay merged, and the adapter
starts from their weights as they were before the merge.

parameters.description: Name of the new adapter; unique among the model's adapters.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage

Build the adapter on the meta device.  Not implemented: `True`
raises `NotImplementedError`.
